final_label: GO step when the history favours a2 (S2 believed good, or a2 chosen last trial)

with_model_outputs.label: GO step where the agent chooses a2
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only on GO steps (100% of activation mass; essentially never on D1 or D2). At GO it fires on 97% of steps where the policy argmax is a2, and its magnitude follows how strongly a2 is preferred: activation correlates about 0.95 with a strongly negative choice logit (logit(a1)-logit(a2)). Every step in the bottom bin (choice < -8.9) is active, and the third and fourth activation quartiles are about 100% covered by the predicate. Misses carry only 4.6% of the mass. They are weak activations (mostly < 0.3 of max) on a1 choices, usually in an a2-leaning context or when the preference for a1 is weak. Not driven by reward, transition type, stay/switch or the reached state beyond their correlation with choosing a2. Recorded model_act (the agent own computed choice at GO); the realized action gives the same F1 (0.888 dev).

issues: The claims hold up. On dev, GO carries 100% of the activation mass. D1 has 54 active steps out of 380k and D2 has 0. On test, the predicate scores P 0.967, R 0.822, F1 0.889 and mass recall 0.954, matching the report. The predicate covers 100% of the 3rd and 4th activation quartiles.

Recall by count is only 0.82. The misses are about 45k test steps, but they hold just 4.6% of the mass. They are a weak, low-level firing on a1 GO steps. They rise with position in the episode: on a1 GO steps the feature is active 15-18% of the time at ep_bucket 3-4 and 32% at ep_bucket 5 (trials 50-99), but always at low magnitude (mass 2.9%). Across runs of repeated a1 choices the activation creeps up slowly (e.g. 0.32 -> 0.37). This is a small baseline drift, not a separate meaning.

The weak a1 firing is concentrated where the a1 preference is weak. On GO & model_act==1 & choice<3, 61% of steps are active, versus 25% overall. This supports reading the feature as a graded 'a2-preference' feature rather than a strict on/off for the a2 choice. A threshold on the logit (GO & choice < 2) does marginally better, with test F1 0.897 and mass recall 0.964.
Adding prev_action==2 (GO & (model_act==2 | prev_action==2)) gives test F1 0.889, no gain. Keeping the simpler predicate is justified.
False positives (about 7k, P 0.967) are scattered. They are slightly more common early in the episode: precision is 0.906 at ep_bucket<=3. No systematic class was found.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step where the agent prefers or chooses a2 (graded by the strength of the a2 preference)

with_model_outputs.final_label: GO step where the agent prefers or chooses a2 (graded by the strength of the a2 preference)

label: GO step when the history favours a2 (S2 believed good, or a2 chosen last trial)
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (100% of mass). Within GO it fires when observed history favours a2: the ideal-observer belief says S2 is more likely good (belief < 0.5), or the agent chose a2 on the previous trial (perseveration). Belief alone gives dev F1 0.82; adding prev_action == 2 raises recall to 0.80 at precision 0.94 (dev F1 0.862; best seen 0.866 with belief < 0.75). Remaining misses are mostly weak activations (0.1-0.3 of max) at GO steps where history favours a1. Magnitude modulation not checked.

issues: Claims check out: 243479/243533 dev activations are at GO; test F1 0.859 (P 0.926, R 0.801).
This is basically an 'upcoming a2 choice' policy feature: (phase==GO)&(choice<1) gets test F1 0.894 and (action==2) 0.888, so the observed history proxy loses about 0.03 F1.

Misses are spread out and weak (7.6% of mass), mostly GO steps after a1 trials where history favours a1. Variants tried (belief<0.6, adding rewarded prev_state==2, a2 two trials back) all stay at 0.856-0.862, so no systematic class was found.
